author: Vox
description:
Democrats will usher in a new era in Washington, after having notched wins in reliably Republican territory. But can the party deliver the affordability relief voters need while facing President Trump?

Democratic strategist David Axelrod, the man behind President Obama’s two White House victories, joins Vox’s Astead Herndon to discuss whether Democrats can turn their midterm wins into a lasting coalition. Axelrod argues the party must work to lower costs and pursue accountability without letting it crowd out the work to improve people’s lives. He also weighs in on the early 2028 field, including JD Vance’s prospects and whether Kamala Harris should run again.

description:
Today we’re bringing you an episode of the Vox daily news podcast Today, Explained. It’s a show that’s about the biggest stories of the day, and – like The Gray Area – it tries to make sense of what those stories tell us about our culture and our world.

Subscribe to our channel! http://goo.gl/0bsAjO

This week, voters delivered a sweeping rebuke to Trump and the Republican party, handing Democrats control of the House and Senate. So this is a good moment to take stock: How did Trump’s brand of politics change America? What has populism actually achieved, who are its new proponents, and are we ever going back?

Host: Noel King, co-host and editorial director, Today, Explained
Guests: Jonathan Chait, staff writer, The Atlantic and Eric Levitz, senior correspondent, Vox
